# Introduction

R Markdown documents in `vitae` use the YAML header to specify document metadata, personal contact information, global document layout settings, and output format options.

Below is a complete example of a YAML header featuring generic `vitae` settings as well as template-specific configuration options.

```yaml
---
title: "Zhenguo Zhang's Resume"
surname: "Zhenguo Zhang"
address: "Irvine, CA"
email: zhangz.sci@gmail.com
phone: +1 814-###-###
www: 'fortune9.netlify.app/home/'
github: fortune9
linkedin: zhenguo-zhang-418b0220
date: "Last updated: `r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`"
papersize: "letterpaper"
fontsize: 10pt
linestretch: 1
geometry: left=0.6in, right=0.6in, top=0.5in, bottom=0.5in
output:
  vitae::crisp:
    show_footer: false
    page_total: false
    keep_tex: true
    keep_md: true
# Crisp-specific options
headcolor: "000000"
spacing_before_section_title: "5pt"
spacing_after_section_title: "-3pt"
classoption: "times"
---
```

---

# General YAML Options

These parameters apply across `vitae` templates and general R Markdown / Pandoc PDF documents.

### Personal Metadata & Contact Info

- **`title`**: The main title of the document (e.g., `"Zhenguo Zhang's Resume"`).
- **`surname`**: The name displayed in the header. Note: when specified, only the surname (or the last word if a full name is provided here) is formatted with a bold font in the header.
- **`address`**: Location or street address to display in the contact header (e.g., `"Irvine, CA"`).
- **`email`**: Email address linked in the header (e.g., `zhangz.sci@gmail.com`).
- **`phone`**: Phone number formatted as a string (e.g., `+1 814-###-###`).
- **`www`**: Personal website or homepage URL (e.g., `'fortune9.netlify.app/home/'`).
- **`github`**: GitHub username (e.g., `fortune9`).
- **`linkedin`**: LinkedIn profile username or slug (e.g., `zhenguo-zhang-418b0220`).
- **`date`**: Date line shown in the header. Supports inline R expressions such as `"Last updated: 'r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')'"`.

### Document Layout & Formatting Options

- **`papersize`**: Paper dimension specification. Common values are `"letterpaper"` or `"a4paper"`.
- **`fontsize`**: Base font size for the document body (e.g., `10pt`, `11pt`, `12pt`).
- **`linestretch`**: Line height multiplier for text spacing (e.g., `1` for single spacing).
- **`geometry`**: Page margins passed to the LaTeX `geometry` package (e.g., `left=0.6in, right=0.6in, top=0.5in, bottom=0.5in`).

### Output Format Options (`vitae::crisp`)

- **`show_footer`**: Boolean (`true` or `false`). Controls whether the footer bar (containing your name and page numbers) is rendered.
- **`page_total`**: Boolean (`true` or `false`). If `true`, shows total page numbers in the footer (e.g., "Page 1 of 2").
- **`keep_tex`**: Boolean (`true` or `false`). Retains the intermediate LaTeX `.tex` file after rendering the PDF.
- **`keep_md`**: Boolean (`true` or `false`). Retains the intermediate Markdown `.md` file after knitr processing.

---

# Crisp Template Specific Options

The `vitae::crisp` template introduces several fine-grained typography and layout options to control header colors, section title margins, and font choices:

- **`headcolor`**: 6-digit hex color code (without `#`) used for the section title accent color (first 3 characters of each section header). For example, `"000000"` sets it to solid black.
- **`spacing_before_section_title`**: A LaTeX length specification (e.g., `"5pt"`, `"1mm"`) determining the vertical space inserted before each section title.
- **`spacing_after_section_title`**: A LaTeX length specification (e.g., `"-3pt"`, `"-1mm"`, `"0.5mm"`) controlling vertical space between a section title and its entries. Negative values tighten the gap.
- **`classoption`**: Specifies font family and template options for `crisp.cls`. Supported font choices include:
  - `"times"`: Uses Times New Roman font family.
  - `"roboto"`: Uses Roboto font family.

---

# Overriding LaTeX Commands and Macros

You can customize or override underlying LaTeX commands and macros directly from your YAML header using the `header-includes` parameter. This allows you to redefine template macros without modifying the `.cls` or `.tex` source files.

For example, to override the default footer layout defined by `\makecvfooter`, add the following snippet to your YAML header:

```yaml
header-includes:
  - |
    \renewcommand*{\makecvfooter}[3]{%
      \fancyfoot{}%
      \fancyfoot[L]{\footerstyle{\href{https://github.com/fortune9/vitae/tree/feat/crisp-template}{Generated by Crisp}}}%
      \fancyfoot[C]{\footerstyle{Zhenguo Zhang}}%
      \fancyfoot[R]{\footerstyle{\thepage}}%
    }
```

This redefines `\makecvfooter` to display a custom link on the left, your name in the center, and the current page number on the right.
